newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on disappointed selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on disappointed selling.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Monday as late disappointed selling swept the market after the main index failed to challenge for a higher upside in early trade, brokers said.
The weighted index, hovered within a narrow range for most of the session but dropped off in the final minutes to close 34.19 points or 0.53 percent lower at 6,424.72.
Turnover was a thin T$30.28 billion.
Investors focused their late selling on the heavily weighted financial sector, which dropped 0.85 percent.
Hua Nan, one of Taiwan's "Big Three" state-run commercial banks, lost 2.78 percent or T$3.50 to T$122.50.
"The slow turnover showed how weak market confidence is, and most investors either stayed on the sidelines or cut their losses," said Eric Liu of National Securities.
Brokers said investment by foreign funds, which is watched closely by the market, was slow due to recent depreciation of the Taiwan dollar against the American currency.
"Foreign investors are less likely to invest in Taiwan stocks if the Taiwan dollar falls too much, and that is a concern right now," Liu said.
Recent central bank announcements that it would not loosen monetary policy also dampened market sentiment, Liu said.
"Investors are a bit concerned that the government is no longer willing to launch measures to further boost the economy," Liu said.

On the other hand, analysts said the market appeared numb to news that the government's index of leading business indicators rose to a "green light" condition in September, the first green light since August 1995 and a sign of a possible recovery.
Brokers expected the index to sink further on Tuesday. A 6,370-6,440 range was seen. -- Kevin Chen (5080815)
